newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end lower but recoup some ground.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end lower but recoup some ground.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips recouped some ground but still finished on Thursday with losses, as underlying bearishness after recent declines kept buyers at bay.
"Everyone has jumped on the bear bandwagon," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp. "Any recovery will be short-lived."

But on the positive front, she noted that volume has been low amid the selloff. The Composite Index of 100 leading stocks ended down 13.07 points or 1.18 percent to 1,096.53, regrouping from a low of 1,091.01 hit earlier.
Volume was extremely thin, topping 176 million shares. Losers swamped gainers by 593 to 66.

"I'm hoping the market stays above 1080," said an equity salesman at W.I. Carr in Hong Kong. He said a myriad of factors was dampening Kuala Lumpur share prices including weakness in the Dow overnight and the possibility of interest rate rises.

Malaysian stocks have been buffetted over the past month by concerns over stricter property and share purchase loans. While investor fears were somewhat later allayed by Bank Negara clarifications, investor sentiment remains bruised, analysts said.
